 Police Station.
 Vs/-

Accused : A1 Vinod M.
 S/o Late Meghendran  A2 Prabhavathi  W/o Late Megendran  A3 Sathish  S/o Late Megendran  A4 Prashanth  S/o Late Megendran  All are residing at No.1938/1, New  No.1-9, 42nd B Cross, Jayanagar, 4th  block, Bengaluru.
 Date of offence : 18-10-2010 to 25-6-2014  2  C.C.No.18203/2015  Offences complained : U/s.498A, 506, 509 r/w/s 34 of  of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of D.P. Act.
 Plea : Accused No.1 to 4 Pleaded not  guilty  Final Order : Accused No.1 to 4 are Acquitted  Date of Order : 01-02-2025.

1  *****
 The Police Sub-Inspector of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against Accused for the offences punishable U/s.
498A, 506, 509 r/w/s 34 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of D.P. Act.
 2.
The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Smt.Poornima.
The gist of the prosecution case is that the Accused No.1 got married to CW-1 on 18-10-2010 at Vasavi Convention center, Basavanagudi as per Customs.

At the time of marriage, as per accused demand, the parents of CW-1 have given 16gms gold chain, 8 gms gold ring, 32 gms gold bracelet, cash of Rs.5 lakhs, suit, watch, 5 kgs worth silver articles to the accused.

After the marriage CW-1 started residing with accused No-1 at Jayanagar 9th block, Shanthi apartment, while staying with him everyday the A2 and A3 induced accused No.1 to do ill will acts against CW-1 and teased CW-1 as dowry given by her parent's is less.
The accused No.1 was not going to job.

Further while staying at No.1938/1, New No.1-9, 42 B cross  3  C.C.No.18203/2015 Jayanagar 4th block, the accused No.1 demanded CW-1 to bring Rs.40 lakhs from her parents house, abused her, assaulted her and while she stayed at her parents house, accused made phone call to get money, her parents have given Rs.2 lakhs to the accused.

The accused No.1 tortured her near her office, snatched her mangalya chain and pledged, tortured her both by physically and mentally thereby accused have committed the offences punishable under Secs. 498(A), 506, 509 r/w 34 of IPC., & Sec. 3 & 4 of D.P. Act.

Based on the said information, a case in Cr.No.33/2014 came to Poornima vs Vinod.M on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49938753/
2 be registered against the accused for the aforesaid offences.
3. After completion of the investigation, the P.SI of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and were enlarged on bail.

The prosecution papers was furnished to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.
 4.

Before framing charge an opportunity of being heard was provided to the accused and after hearing them and the prosecution and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offences was framed and same was read over to the
4  C.C.No.18203/2015 accused in the language known to them, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The plea of the accused was recorded.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 and P.2 documents.

The Statement of Accused No.1 to 4 as required U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C.,
was recorded.
The accused No.1 to 4 denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against them.
The accused No.1 to 4 have not let in any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
6. Heard arguments on both the sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

Poornima vs Vinod.M on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49938753/
3  7.

The following points arise for my determination:-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the accused persons caused physical and  mental cruelty to the complainant in demand of dowry  abused her in filthy language and threatened to kill her  and thereby accused have committed the offences  punishable U/s. 498(A), 506, 509 r/w 34 of IPC., & Sec.
 3 & 4 of D.P. Act?
2) what order?

8. My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 ........In the Negative.
 5  C.C.No.18203/2015  Point No.2........

As per final order, for the following:
 REASONS  9. POINT No.1 :- It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

In order to bring home the guilt of the accused,
the prosecution has examined one witness as CW-7/PW-1 Kavitha G.M..
She has deposed in her evidence that on 23-09-2014 she took further investigation of this case from CW6 and continued the investigation.
On 21-10-2014 recorded statement of complainant after completion of the investigation she submitted chargesheet against accused persons.
10. On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is apparent that CW-1 being the informant, key and material witness has not appeared before court to depose about the incident.
CW7 who was examined as PW-1 has deposed about the investigation done by her
is only a formal in nature.

The only evidence available Poornima vs Vinod.M on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49938753/
4 on record is insufficient to prove the allegations made against the accused.
In the absence of evidence of material witnesses, the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused  6  C.C.No.18203/2015 beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

11. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER

In exercise of power conferred Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., accused No.1 to 4 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 498(A), 506, 509 r/w 34 of IPC., & Sec. 3 & 4 of D.P. Act The bail bonds of accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force for a period of 6 months.

(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on the computer and print out taken by her is verified,
corrected & then pronounced by me in the Open Court dated this the 01-02-2025).
(SYED ARFATH IBRAHIM M.) XXXVII ACJM., BENGALURU.
